title: Flowing conjecture
formal: Is every minimally nonideal binary clutter isomorphic to exactly one of the three obstruction types specified below: the Fano-line clutter, the odd-circuit clutter of K5, or the clutter of complements of nontrivial cuts of K5?
definitions:
A clutter is a finite family of subsets of a finite ground set E with no member properly containing another. Its blocker is the family of inclusion-minimal subsets of E meeting every member. A clutter is binary if the intersection of every member with every member of its blocker has odd cardinality. It is ideal if {x≥0: sum over e in S of x_e≥1 for every member S} is an integral polyhedron, meaning it is the convex hull of its integer points; the empty polyhedron is integral. Deletion of e discards members containing e; contraction removes e from every member and then retains only inclusion-minimal sets. Both operations remove e from the ground set. Minimally nonideal means nonideal with every proper minor obtained by at least one deletion or contraction ideal.

The Fano-line clutter has ground set F_2^3 minus the zero vector, with the seven triples {u,v,u+v} for distinct nonzero u,v; addition is coordinatewise modulo two. The second ground set is the ten edges of the complete simple graph on five vertices; its members are edge sets of simple cycles of length three or five. On the same ground set, the third clutter has members E(K5) minus delta(U) for every nonempty proper vertex subset U, removing duplicate sets, where delta(U) consists of edges with one endpoint in U. Equivalently these members are a K4 on four vertices or a triangle together with the edge on the other two vertices. Isomorphism is a bijection of ground sets carrying members to members.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the obstruction classification, including that the listed clutters are minimally nonideal and binary, or a counterexample to the classification. Replacing the third family by complements of arbitrary edge sets changes the target.
context: Guenin’s author-hosted formulation lists the three explicit obstructions and describes graphical special cases. It also explains their relationship through blocking.
why: A forbidden-minor characterization would explain integrality across a central class of covering problems.

import_provenance.original_title: The Flowing conjecture for ideal binary clutters
import_provenance.original_statement: Is every binary clutter ideal exactly when it has none of the three forbidden minors: the Fano-plane line clutter, the odd-circuit clutter of K5, and the blocker of the latter? Equivalently, are these the only minimally nonideal binary clutters, giving a complete structural criterion for integral covering.
